rationale: Firms investing heavily in marketing may be able to build brand and drive future growth, or may be compensating for weak products.

name: CEO Tenure
construction: Number of years since the most recent CEO appointment (from company filings and annual reports).
rationale: Longer-tenured CEOs may indicate management stability, while very new CEOs might signal upcoming strategic change or risk.

name: Downward Earnings Revision Frequency
construction: Count of downward changes in consensus analyst earnings estimates (I/B/E/S data) over the previous 12 months.
rationale: Frequent negative earnings revisions may indicate deteriorating fundamentals unpriced by the market.

name: Asset Sale Frequency
construction: Number of non-core asset sales (disclosed in 10-K or press releases) in past two years.
rationale: Frequent asset sales could signal attempts to boost short-term results or financial stress.

name: Patent Count Growth
construction: Percentage growth in cumulative US patents granted to the firm over the past three years (USPTO data).
rationale: Increasing patent counts may indicate innovation pipelines that drive future growth.

name: Dividend Omission Indicator
construction: Binary indicator equal to one if the firm has omitted a regular cash dividend in the past year.
rationale: Dividend omissions may be a distress signal not fully reflected in stock prices.

name: Year-over-Year Insider Net Buying
construction: Net number of shares bought by insiders (officer and director Form 4 filings) over the prior 12 months, scaled by shares outstanding.
rationale: Insider buying can signal undervaluation or managerial confidence in future prospects.

name: Short-Term Earnings Acceleration
construction: Compute the change in quarterly earnings growth rate: (most recent quarterly EPS - EPS one quarter ago) minus (EPS one quarter ago - EPS two quarters ago), divided by stock price. Use data from quarterly filings.
rationale: Rapid acceleration in earnings growth may signal improving prospects not yet fully priced in.

name: Net Buyback Yield
construction: Annual net share repurchases divided by market capitalization, using Compustat data for shares outstanding and CRSP for market cap.
rationale: Firms reducing share count may be signaling undervaluation or strong cash flows.

name: Labor Efficiency Ratio
construction: Annual sales per employee (from Compustat) divided by total assets.
rationale: Firms generating more revenue per employee relative to their asset base may be more efficient and profitable.

name: Inventory Change Scaled by Sales
construction: Annual change in inventories divided by annual sales, both from Compustat.
rationale: Rising inventories relative to sales may signal demand overestimation and future underperformance.

name: Insider Buying Concentration
construction: Number of shares purchased by insiders in the past 6 months divided by total shares outstanding, using SEC Form 4 filings.
rationale: Substantial insider buying may reflect private information about future prospects.

name: Deferred Tax Asset Ratio
construction: Total deferred tax assets divided by total assets, from Compustat annual statements.
rationale: Low levels may indicate aggressive revenue recognition or fewer tax shields, possibly linked to conservative accounting.

name: Long-Term Debt Maturity Proximity
construction: Portion of long-term debt due within next 2 years divided by total long-term debt, from Compustat.
rationale: Imminent debt maturities may create refinancing risk, affecting future returns.

name: Gross Profitability to Market
construction: Gross profit (sales minus cost of goods sold) over the past 12 months divided by market capitalization.
rationale: Firms with higher gross profitability relative to price may be undervalued.

name: R&D Scaling Ratio
construction: Annual R&D expense divided by total assets, from Compustat.
rationale: Firms investing more in R&D may experience future innovations and growth not yet priced in.

name: Change in Working Capital Ratio
construction: Annual change in net working capital divided by total assets, calculated from balance sheet data.
rationale: A declining working capital ratio may indicate improving operational efficiency.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth
construction: Percentage change in total assets (Compustat ATQ) over the most recent fiscal quarter.
rationale: Rapid asset growth may indicate empire building or overinvestment, potentially leading to lower future returns due to inefficient capital deployment.

name: Operating Expense Ratio
construction: Total operating expenses (Compustat XOPR) divided by total revenues (Compustat REVT) from the latest annual report.
rationale: Firms with higher operating efficiency may generate better margins and be more competitively positioned, leading to superior returns.

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: Cumulative R&D expenditures (Compustat XRD) over past 3 years divided by total assets (Compustat AT) at the latest fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms investing more in R&D may be positioned for innovation-driven growth and higher future returns.

name: Inventory Turnover Acceleration
construction: Change in inventory turnover ratio (annual cost of goods sold (COGS, Compustat COGS) divided by average inventories (Compustat INVT)) over the past two years.
rationale: Improving inventory management may indicate operational improvements and demand strength.

name: Net Insider Buying
construction: Net shares bought by insiders over the past 6 months, from SEC Form 4 filings, scaled by shares outstanding.
rationale: Executives with superior information may buy stock ahead of positive developments, signaling undervaluation.

name: Capex Deviation
construction: Current year's capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX) minus average of previous three years' CAPX, scaled by total assets (Compustat AT).
rationale: Sudden increases or decreases in investment may signal strategic shifts; negative deviations could reflect caution or underinvestment, while positive may reflect over-optimism.
higher_returns_for: moderate or near-zero values of the measure

name: Dividend Omission Indicator
construction: Dummy variable: 1 if a company paid dividends last year, but omitted dividends this year; 0 otherwise (Compustat DV/annual reports).
rationale: Dividend omission often signals financial distress, which may lead to higher required returns as compensation for risk.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (i.e., recent dividend omissions)

name: Late 10-K Filing Flag
construction: Dummy variable: 1 if the company files its annual 10-K report later than the SEC deadline; 0 otherwise (public SEC EDGAR data).
rationale: Late filings may signal accounting or operational issues, which could increase risk and expected returns.
higher_returns_for: high values of the measure (i.e., late filers)

name: Earnings Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly earnings per share (EPS, Compustat EPSPX) over the last eight quarters.
rationale: Higher earnings volatility may indicate business risk, leading to higher required compensation.

name: Analyst Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of one-year-ahead EPS forecasts across analysts (I/B/E/S) at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Greater disagreement among analysts may signal higher uncertainty and risk, potentially leading to higher required returns.

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in total number of employees, using headcount data from annual 10-K filings.
rationale: Rapid expansion in workforce may signal aggressive growth strategies or overinvestment; lower growth could reflect discipline or maturity.

name: Inventory Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly inventory levels over the past three years, divided by average total assets.
rationale: High inventory volatility might indicate demand uncertainty or operational inefficiency, which could be penalized by investors.

name: Operating Lease Intensity
construction: Total annual operating lease expense divided by total assets, from annual financial statements.
rationale: Firms with high off-balance-sheet leverage may be riskier than they appear, potentially offering higher returns.

name: Long-Term Debt Repayment Ratio
construction: Ratio of principal repayments of long-term debt in the past year to total long-term debt outstanding.
rationale: Firms aggressively paying down debt may be signaling robust cash flows and prudent management, potentially yielding higher future returns.

name: SG&A Efficiency Ratio
construction: One minus the ratio of selling, general, and administrative expenses to gross profit, using annual data.
rationale: A higher ratio indicates better cost control relative to gross profit, possibly leading to superior profitability and returns.

name: Patent Count Change
construction: Annual percentage change in the number of patents granted to the company (using USPTO data matched by firm name or CUSIP).
rationale: Increasing patent activity may signal innovation and future growth potential.

name: Net Non-Operating Income Ratio
construction: Non-operating income (such as from investments or asset sales) less non-operating expenses, divided by total income before extraordinary items, using annual income statements.
rationale: Firms that rely less on non-operating income may have more sustainable core earnings.

name: Foreign Sales Proportion
construction: Total foreign sales divided by total sales, as reported in segment disclosures in 10-K filings.
rationale: Greater international exposure may diversify revenue sources and offer growth opportunities, especially for US investors.

name: Receivables Turnover Change
construction: Year-over-year change in receivables turnover ratio (annual credit sales divided by average accounts receivable).
rationale: Improvement in receivables turnover suggests better cash collection and working capital management.

name: CEO Tenure
construction: Number of years since current CEO assumed office, using executive disclosures in proxy statements (DEF 14A).
rationale: Very short tenures may indicate instability; very long tenures could signal entrenchment. Recent appointments may involve significant strategic change and risk.

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Change in R&D expenditure over the past year, scaled by beginning-of-year total assets. Data from Compustat: (R&D_t - R&D_{t-1}) / Assets_{t-1}.
rationale: Firms increasing R&D investment may have better growth prospects not yet fully priced by the market.

name: Short-Term Debt Surge
construction: Percentage increase in short-term debt (Compustat: Data item 34) over the past fiscal year.
rationale: Sudden increases in short-term borrowing might signal liquidity needs or aggressive expansion, potentially leading to higher future returns if those bets succeed.

name: Inventory Turnover Acceleration
construction: One-year change in inventory turnover ratio: (COGS / Average Inventory)_{t} - (COGS / Average Inventory)_{t-1}.
rationale: Improving inventory turnover may indicate operational improvements or increasing demand, both of which can foreshadow higher returns.

name: Insider Net Purchase Ratio
construction: Net number of shares acquired by insiders over the past year, divided by shares outstanding. Source: SEC insider filings.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect management’s confidence in future prospects.

name: Non-Operating Income Share
construction: Proportion of pre-tax income from non-operating sources (non-operating income / pre-tax income, Compustat items 13/170).
rationale: A high share may signal low earnings quality and risk of negative surprises.

name: Unexpected Dividend Initiations
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if the firm paid a dividend this year but none in the prior three years, 0 otherwise.
rationale: Surprise dividend initiations may signal management’s confidence in sustainable cash flows.

name: Patent Count Growth
construction: Percentage change in the number of US patents granted (USPTO data) in the last three years relative to the prior three years.
rationale: Rapid innovation, as evidenced by patenting activity, may foreshadow future profitability and returns.

name: Related-Party Transactions Ratio
construction: Dollar value of disclosed related-party transactions (from annual report footnotes) divided by total assets.
rationale: High levels may indicate potential agency conflicts and lower future returns.

name: Auditor Tenure Change
construction: Binary variable: 1 if auditor changed in the past fiscal year, 0 otherwise (from proxy statements).
rationale: Recent auditor changes may signal forthcoming accounting restatements or firm-specific shocks.

name: Post-Listing Return Reversal
construction: Cumulative abnormal return in months 7-12 after IPO or exchange listing (adjusted for market return).
rationale: Initial post-listing overreaction may reverse, providing higher returns to laggard stocks.

name: Operating Expense Efficiency
construction: Total operating expenses (from income statement) divided by total revenues, measured over the trailing twelve months.
rationale: Firms with lower operating expense ratios may have better cost controls, potentially leading to higher profitability and investor re-rating.

name: Inventory Accruals
construction: Change in inventories (from balance sheet) over the past year divided by average total assets.
rationale: High inventory accruals can signal aggressive revenue recognition or slowing demand, which may foreshadow weaker future performance.

name: Dividend Change Momentum
construction: Percentage change in annual dividends per share over the past three years.
rationale: Firms with accelerating dividend growth may be signaling strong, sustainable cash flows and commitment to shareholders.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth
construction: Change in current assets (from balance sheet) over the past year divided by lagged total assets.
rationale: Rapid asset growth can be associated with overinvestment or empire-building, which may lead to lower subsequent returns.

name: SG&A Intensity
construction: Selling, general, and administrative (SG&A) expenses divided by total revenues, measured over the trailing twelve months.
rationale: Lower SG&A intensity may indicate more efficient operations and better margin discipline.

name: Relative Analyst Coverage
construction: Number of analyst earnings estimates for a firm divided by the median number for its industry (data from I/B/E/S or similar).
rationale: Stocks with less analyst attention may be more likely to be mispriced, offering higher average returns to investors who do the extra research.

name: Late Reporter Penalty
construction: Number of days between fiscal year-end and annual report (10-K) filing date.
rationale: Firms that delay financial reporting may have poor internal controls or negative surprises, both factors that could predict lower future returns.

name: Net Insider Purchases
construction: Net number of shares purchased by insiders over the prior six months, scaled by shares outstanding (data from SEC filings).
rationale: Insider buying may indicate undervaluation or confidence in firm prospects, while selling can signal the opposite.

name: Interest Coverage Change
construction: Change in earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) divided by interest expense, comparing the most recent year to the previous year.
rationale: Improvement in the ability to service debt may indicate strengthening financial health, which could lead to higher future returns.

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: Total R&D expense over the past three years divided by average total assets, for firms that capitalize and expense R&D (where disclosed).
rationale: Firms investing more heavily in R&D relative to assets may generate higher innovation and long-term growth, which the market might underappreciate.

name: Short-Term Operating Leverage
construction: Change in operating income divided by change in sales over the past 12 months, as reported in quarterly filings.
rationale: Firms with high operating leverage are more sensitive to economic shocks, which may be underappreciated and thus mispriced by investors.

name: Inventory Growth Deceleration
construction: One-year change in inventory growth rate: (Inventory_t - Inventory_{t-1}) / Inventory_{t-1} minus (Inventory_{t-1} - Inventory_{t-2}) / Inventory_{t-2}, using annual Compustat items.
rationale: A deceleration in inventory growth may signal improving demand-supply balance and potential positive future surprises.

name: Seasonal Sales Momentum
construction: Sales growth in the most recent fiscal quarter relative to the same quarter last year: (Sales_{q,t} - Sales_{q,t-4}) / Sales_{q,t-4}.
rationale: Seasonal patterns in sales growth may provide more timely signals about business momentum than annual growth rates.

name: Dividend Omission Indicator
construction: A binary variable indicating whether a firm has omitted dividends this year after paying in each of the previous three years.
rationale: Dividend omissions may be viewed overly negatively by the market, resulting in return reversals for omitted firms.

name: Relative Employee Productivity
construction: Total sales over the past year divided by the number of employees (from 10-K filings), normalized by industry median.
rationale: Higher productivity may indicate better management practices or operational efficiency not yet reflected in prices.
higher_returns_for: high values relative to industry median

name: Deferred Tax Asset Ratio
construction: Deferred tax assets divided by total assets, from the most recent annual balance sheet.
rationale: Firms with high deferred tax assets might have future tax shields leading to higher after-tax profits.

name: Insider Option Grant Intensity
construction: Number of stock options granted to insiders over the past 12 months divided by shares outstanding, as reported in proxy statements.
rationale: Large insider grants may signal undervaluation or future growth expectations that external investors have not yet priced in.

name: Receivables Accruals Ratio
construction: Change in accounts receivable over the past year divided by average total assets, from annual financial statements.
rationale: Receivables growth may indicate aggressive revenue recognition, which can predict lower future returns if overestimated.

name: R&D Intensity Surprise
construction: Current year R&D expenditure divided by sales, minus the mean of this ratio over the prior three years.
rationale: A sudden jump in R&D intensity may signal new growth initiatives or product cycles not yet recognized by the market.

name: Supplier Concentration Ratio
construction: Sum of the top three suppliers' purchase percentages (from 10-K disclosures) as a fraction of total purchases.
rationale: Firms with low supplier concentration may have more bargaining power and supply chain resilience, which could boost future returns.

name: Short-Term Earnings Acceleration
construction: Difference between the most recent quarter's year-over-year earnings growth rate and the previous quarter's year-over-year earnings growth rate, using Compustat quarterly earnings data.
rationale: Firms with accelerating earnings growth may signal improved fundamentals not yet reflected in prices.

name: Unexpected Inventory Change
construction: Current quarter's change in inventory (from Compustat) minus average quarterly inventory change over the past 8 quarters, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Unexpected inventory buildups or drawdowns may indicate future sales surprises or supply chain signals.

name: Cash Flow Over Accruals
construction: Ratio of operating cash flow (from Statement of Cash Flows) to total accruals (earnings minus cash flow), measured over the trailing four quarters.
rationale: Firms generating a larger share of their earnings in cash may be less prone to earnings manipulation and future disappointments.

name: Insider Purchase Intensity
construction: Number of shares purchased by insiders over the past six months divided by total shares outstanding, using SEC Form 4 data.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect private information about undervaluation or positive future prospects.

name: R&D to Capex Shift
construction: Change in the ratio of R&D expense to capital expenditures over the past three years, using Compustat annual data.
rationale: A shift toward R&D investment may signal a firm’s strategic pivot to high-growth opportunities.
higher_returns_for: high positive changes in the measure

name: Relative Analyst Forecast Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of one-year-ahead analyst earnings forecasts divided by mean forecast, using I/B/E/S data, relative to the firm’s own 3-year history.
rationale: Decreasing forecast dispersion relative to history may indicate emerging consensus and reduced uncertainty.
higher_returns_for: firms with lower current dispersion vs their own history

name: Deferred Tax Asset Proportion
construction: Deferred tax assets as a percent of total assets, from Compustat annual data.
rationale: High deferred tax assets may reflect aggressive accounting or persistent losses, potentially predicting lower returns.
higher_returns_for: firms with low values of the measure

name: Gross Margin Stability
construction: Standard deviation of gross margin (gross profit/sales) over trailing 12 quarters.
rationale: Stable gross margins may indicate strong competitive positioning and pricing power.
higher_returns_for: firms with low values of the measure

name: Share Repurchase Yield
construction: Cash spent on share repurchases during the past year divided by average market capitalization, using Compustat and CRSP data.
rationale: Firms actively repurchasing shares may signal undervaluation or confidence in future cash flows.

name: Dividend Initiation Signal
construction: Binary indicator for firms that initiate a regular cash dividend in the past four quarters (Compustat dividend data).
rationale: Dividend initiation can serve as a signal of management’s confidence in future profitability and cash flows.
higher_returns_for: firms that recently initiated a dividend

name: Inventory Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in inventories (from Compustat annual data: INVT) divided by prior-year total assets (AT).
rationale: Firms aggressively building inventories may be overestimating future demand, leading to subsequent corrections.

name: Short-Term Debt Surge
construction: Current year increase in short-term debt (DLC) scaled by total assets (AT), using Compustat annual data.
rationale: A surge in short-term borrowing may signal liquidity stress or poor credit conditions.

name: Non-Operating Income Share
construction: Non-operating income (OIBDP - OIADP) divided by total revenues (REVT), using Compustat annual data.
rationale: A high reliance on non-core activities may indicate lower earnings quality and higher risk.

name: Past Insider Buying
construction: Net shares bought by insiders (Form 4 SEC filings), aggregated over the prior 12 months and scaled by shares outstanding.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect superior information regarding undervaluation or positive future prospects.

name: Dividend Omission Indicator
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if a firm paid dividends two years ago but omitted dividends in the most recent fiscal year (from CRSP/Compustat).
rationale: Omitting a dividend may signal financial distress or deteriorating fundamentals.
higher_returns_for: firms without recent omissions (i.e., a value of 0)

name: Seasonal Sales Momentum
construction: Current quarter sales (SALEQ) minus sales from the same quarter last year, scaled by prior-year quarterly sales (Compustat quarterly data).
rationale: Unexpected improvement in seasonal sales may indicate underestimated growth potential.

name: R&D Expense Growth
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in R&D expense (XRD) divided by prior-year total assets (AT), using Compustat annual data.
rationale: Accelerating investment in R&D may signal innovation and future profitability.

name: Dividend Payout Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of annual dividend per share (DPS, CRSP) over the past five years divided by mean DPS.
rationale: High dividend volatility may indicate unstable earnings or weak governance.

name: Cash Acquisition Ratio
construction: Cash used for acquisitions (from Statement of Cash Flows, Compustat CHEQ outflows for acquisitions) divided by total assets (AT), over trailing three years.
rationale: Aggressive acquisition activity may lead to post-merger integration risk and lower returns.

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in number of employees (EMP, Compustat annual data), divided by prior-year employees.
rationale: Rapid hiring may reflect overexpansion or management optimism that outpaces market reality.

name: Inventory Growth
construction: Calculate the year-over-year percentage change in inventories from Compustat annual data: (Inventories_t - Inventories_{t-1}) / Inventories_{t-1}.
rationale: Rising inventories may signal slowing demand or over-optimism by management, while shrinking inventories may reflect strong sales or conservative management.

name: Short-Term Debt to Total Assets
construction: Divide short-term debt (Compustat: Debt in Current Liabilities) by total assets, measured at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms with higher reliance on short-term debt may face refinancing risk and financial distress, while low ratios indicate stability.

name: Receivables to Sales Ratio
construction: Compute accounts receivable (Compustat) divided by net sales (Compustat) for the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: A high ratio could point to aggressive revenue recognition or deteriorating customer quality.

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Calculate the annual change in R&D expenditure-to-sales ratio: (R&D_t / Sales_t) - (R&D_{t-1} / Sales_{t-1}).
rationale: Rising R&D intensity may signal increased investment in future growth opportunities.

name: Dividend Deviation
construction: Take the absolute difference between the most recent annual dividend and the three-year average dividend, divided by the three-year average dividend.
rationale: Unusually large changes in dividend policy may indicate information about future prospects or risk.

name: Cash Flow Skewness
construction: Compute the skewness of quarterly operating cash flows over the past three years (12 quarters) for each firm.
rationale: Firms with large positive or negative skew in cash flows may be subject to unusual events or earnings management.

name: Gross Margin Expansion
construction: The change in gross margin (gross profit divided by sales) from the prior fiscal year to the current year.
rationale: Improving gross margins may indicate strengthening competitive position or operational efficiency.

name: SG&A to Sales Decline
construction: Measure the year-over-year change in SG&A expense divided by sales, using Compustat annual data.
rationale: Firms that are effectively controlling overhead (declining SG&A/Sales) may achieve higher profitability.

name: Net Insider Buying
construction: Sum net insider purchases (Form 4 filings, SEC) over the past 12 months, scaled by shares outstanding.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect superior private information regarding firm prospects.

name: Sales Volatility
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly sales growth rates over the past three years (12 quarters).
rationale: High sales volatility may indicate unpredictable fundamentals and higher risk.

name: Inventory Growth Rate
construction: Annual percentage change in inventory (Compustat item INVQ) over the past fiscal year.
rationale: Rapid inventory accumulation may signal over-optimism or demand overestimation, while slow or negative growth may indicate prudent management or strong sales.

name: Short-Term Debt to Total Assets
construction: Ratio of short-term debt (Compustat item DLCQ) to total assets (Compustat item ATQ) at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms with higher short-term leverage may face refinancing risk and financial distress, while lower ratios suggest more stable capital structures.

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Change in R&D expense (Compustat item XRDQ) as a percentage of sales (Compustat item SALEQ) over the past two fiscal years.
rationale: Increasing R&D intensity may signal management's confidence in future growth opportunities.

name: Operating Cash Flow Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly operating cash flow (Compustat item OANCF) over the past 8 quarters.
rationale: Lower volatility in operating cash flows may indicate more stable and predictable businesses.

name: Net Insider Buying Ratio
construction: Net shares purchased by insiders (Form 4 filings, SEC) over the past 12 months divided by total shares outstanding.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect private information about undervaluation or positive prospects.

name: Dividend Initiation Dummy
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if a firm initiates a regular cash dividend in the past 12 months, 0 otherwise.
rationale: Dividend initiations may signal management's confidence in sustainable future earnings.

name: Customer Concentration
construction: Sum of sales to top three customers (from 10-K disclosures) divided by total sales for the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: High customer concentration increases business risk due to reliance on a few clients.

name: Employee Productivity Growth
construction: Annual percentage change in sales (Compustat item SALEQ) per employee (from 10-K headcount disclosures) over the past year.
rationale: Improving productivity may reflect operational efficiency and competitive advantage.

name: Deferred Tax Asset Ratio
construction: Deferred tax assets (Compustat item TXDB) divided by total assets (Compustat item ATQ) at fiscal year-end.
rationale: High deferred tax assets may indicate aggressive accounting or past unprofitable operations.

name: Seasonal Sales Growth
construction: Percentage change in sales (Compustat item SALEQ) from the same fiscal quarter in the prior year.
rationale: Strong year-over-year quarterly sales growth may signal robust demand and momentum.

name: Inventory Adjustment Ratio
construction: Annual change in inventories divided by prior year total assets (from Compustat).
rationale: Firms with large inventory reductions may signal operational efficiency or demand shocks, potentially impacting future profitability.
higher_returns_for: firms with high negative (large reductions) inventory adjustment ratios

name: Quarterly Insider Option Exercise Rate
construction: Number of stock options exercised by insiders in the previous quarter (from SEC filings) divided by the number of options outstanding.
rationale: High exercise rates may indicate insiders believe the stock is fairly or overvalued, while low rates could indicate undervaluation.
higher_returns_for: firms with low insider option exercise rates

name: Dividend Smoothing Index
construction: Standard deviation of annual dividend per share over the past 5 years divided by mean dividend per share (from CRSP/Compustat).
rationale: Lower variability may signal stable management and reliable cash flows, while higher variability may point to riskier future prospects.
higher_returns_for: firms with low dividend smoothing index

name: R&D Scaling Factor
construction: R&D expense (Compustat item XRD) divided by current market capitalization.
rationale: Firms investing heavily in R&D relative to their size may have greater growth opportunities, not fully priced by the market.
higher_returns_for: firms with high R&D scaling factor

name: Short-Term Asset Turnover Change
construction: Change in asset turnover ratio (sales/total assets) from previous year to current year.
rationale: Improving asset turnover may reflect enhanced operational efficiency, which could lead to higher future returns.
higher_returns_for: firms with large positive changes in asset turnover

name: Negative Earnings Surprise Persistence
construction: Count of consecutive quarters with negative earnings surprises (actual EPS below consensus, from I/B/E/S) over past 2 years.
rationale: Extended negative surprises might result in undervaluation due to market overreaction.
higher_returns_for: firms with high counts of negative earnings surprise persistence

name: Late 10-K Filing Penalty
construction: Indicator variable for firms filing 10-K reports more than 90 days after fiscal year-end (SEC/EDGAR data).
rationale: Late filings may indicate accounting or operational troubles, but may also lead to excessive discounting by the market.

name: Long-Term Depreciation Policy Aggressiveness
construction: Ratio of accumulated depreciation to gross property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) over the past 10 years.
rationale: Aggressive depreciation could create hidden value by understating book assets and earnings.
higher_returns_for: firms with high depreciation policy aggressiveness ratio

name: Supplier Concentration Index
construction: Top supplier purchases divided by total purchases (from 10-K segment disclosures or industry sources).
rationale: High concentration may expose firms to idiosyncratic risk, affecting future returns depending on market perception.
higher_returns_for: firms with low supplier concentration index

name: CEO Tenure Stability
construction: Number of consecutive years current CEO has held position, from annual reports.
rationale: Stable leadership may foster long-term strategies that are undervalued by the market.
higher_returns_for: firms with high CEO tenure stability

name: Short-Term Earnings Acceleration
construction: Compute the change in quarterly earnings growth rate: (most recent quarterly EPS - EPS one quarter ago) minus (EPS one quarter ago - EPS two quarters ago), divided by stock price. Use data from quarterly filings.
rationale: Rapid acceleration in earnings growth may signal underappreciated improvement in fundamentals not yet reflected in prices.

name: Net Debt Change Yield
construction: Calculate (total debt minus cash and short-term investments) change over the past year, divided by market capitalization.
rationale: Firms reducing net debt may be improving balance sheet strength, which could lead to higher subsequent returns if the market under-reacts.
higher_returns_for: large negative values of the measure

name: Employee Efficiency Ratio
construction: Total annual sales divided by number of employees (from 10-K), then divided by market capitalization.
rationale: Firms with greater sales per employee relative to their market value may be more operationally efficient and undervalued by investors.

name: Recent Insider Transaction Ratio
construction: Sum of net purchases (insider buys minus sells) over the last 6 months, divided by shares outstanding.
rationale: Net insider buying may indicate undervaluation or positive private information not yet reflected in the price.

name: Off-Balance Sheet Commitment Ratio
construction: Estimated future operating lease commitments (disclosed in footnotes) divided by total assets.
rationale: Firms with lower off-balance sheet liabilities may have less hidden leverage risk, potentially leading to higher future returns.

name: Late Filer Flag
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if the most recent 10-K or 10-Q filing was delayed beyond SEC deadline by more than 7 days, 0 otherwise.
rationale: Delayed filings may signal financial distress or management issues, likely penalized by the market.

name: Within-Industry Dividend Initiator
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if the firm initiated a dividend in the last year, and its industry peer group dividend initiation rate is below the median.
rationale: Dividend initiations in low-dividend industries may provide a stronger positive signal of financial health and confidence.

name: Preliminary Earnings Guidance Surprise
construction: Difference between most recent management preliminary earnings guidance and consensus analyst forecast, divided by stock price.
rationale: Positive surprises in guidance may go underappreciated by the market and predict outperformance.

name: Inventory Write-Down Frequency
construction: Count of inventory write-downs taken in the last three years, from 10-K notes.
rationale: Frequent inventory write-downs may indicate persistent operational inefficiencies or demand misestimation.

name: Relative Auditor Tenure
construction: Years with current auditor divided by industry average auditor tenure.
rationale: Unusually short auditor tenures may be associated with riskier or less transparent firms.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth Reversal
construction: Compute percentage change in total assets over the most recent quarter, then reverse-sort: focus on stocks with the largest declines in assets over the past quarter.
rationale: Firms rapidly reducing assets may be recovering from overinvestment or divesting unproductive segments, potentially boosting future performance.
higher_returns_for: stocks with the most negative recent quarterly asset growth

name: R&D to Gross Margin Ratio
construction: Divide a company’s annual research & development expense by its trailing twelve-month gross margin.
rationale: High R&D spend relative to gross profits may indicate strong reinvestment in innovation and long-term competitive advantage.

name: Inventory Write-Down Ratio
construction: Sum inventory write-downs reported over the past year, divide by average total inventory for the same period.
rationale: Firms recognizing inventory obsolescence promptly may have more conservative accounting and better risk management, positioning for recovery.

name: Late Accounts Receivable Growth
construction: Calculate the 12-month change in accounts receivable, scaled by sales; focus on the top decile of increases.
rationale: Unusual growth in accounts receivable relative to sales may signal aggressive revenue recognition and higher risk, so lower growth may be positive.

name: Net Repurchase Yield
construction: Total cash spent on share buybacks minus cash received from share issuance, divided by market capitalization, over the past year.
rationale: Firms that shrink their share count may signal confidence in undervaluation and shareholder alignment.

name: Employee Efficiency Ratio
construction: Calculate total revenue divided by the number of employees; use the year-over-year change in this ratio.
rationale: Rising revenue per employee can indicate operational efficiency improvements that may translate into higher profitability.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Dummy variable equal to one for firms that initiated a dividend (paid a first dividend) in the past 12 months.
rationale: Firms beginning to pay dividends may have reached a new level of financial stability or profitability, signaling positive prospects.

name: Tax Rate Deviation
construction: Difference between the effective tax rate and the statutory federal tax rate, averaged over the past two years.
rationale: Firms with lower effective tax rates than the statutory rate may benefit from persistent tax advantages, raising future net income.

name: Minority Interest Growth
construction: 12-month percentage change in minority interest reported on the balance sheet.
rationale: Rising minority interest may indicate profitable expansion of consolidated subsidiaries or joint ventures.

name: Deferred Revenue Ratio
construction: Deferred revenue at fiscal year-end divided by total assets.
rationale: High deferred revenue may signal strong future sales and cash flow visibility, supporting higher valuations.

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in total number of employees, using headcount data from annual 10-K filings.
rationale: Rapid expansion in workforce may signal aggressive growth strategies or overinvestment; lower or negative growth may indicate operational efficiency or retrenchment.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative employee growth rates

name: Net Insider Option Grants
construction: Total number of stock options granted to insiders minus options exercised by insiders over the past twelve months, scaled by total shares outstanding.
rationale: A high net grant may signal management's confidence in undervaluation or, alternatively, potential dilution; low or negative net grants may reflect insider skepticism.
higher_returns_for: firms with high net insider option grants

name: Inter-Industry Sales Exposure
construction: Percentage of revenues derived from sales to firms outside the company’s primary SIC industry, as disclosed in segment reporting.
rationale: High exposure may indicate diversification benefits or lack of focus; low exposure may reflect industry specialization and competitive advantage.
higher_returns_for: firms with low inter-industry sales exposure

name: Short-Term Accruals Ratio
construction: (Change in current assets - change in current liabilities - change in cash + change in short-term debt) divided by average total assets over the past year.
rationale: High short-term accruals may reflect earnings management and lower earnings quality, leading to lower future returns.
higher_returns_for: firms with low short-term accruals ratios

name: Supplier Concentration Risk
construction: Percentage of cost of goods sold paid to the single largest supplier, as disclosed in 10-K footnotes.
rationale: Dependence on a single supplier may increase operational risk and reduce bargaining power, impacting long-term profitability.
higher_returns_for: firms with low supplier concentration risk

name: Effective Tax Rate Deviation
construction: Absolute difference between the firm’s effective tax rate and the median effective tax rate for its SIC peer group, based on most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Large deviations may signal tax avoidance or inefficiency, possibly affecting sustainability of reported earnings.
higher_returns_for: firms with low effective tax rate deviation

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: Cumulative R&D expense over the past five years divided by the sum of annual depreciation and amortization over the same period.
rationale: High ratios may indicate heavy investment in intangible assets not reflected on the balance sheet, potentially underappreciated by the market.
higher_returns_for: firms with high R&D capitalization ratios

name: Board Tenure Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of years of tenure among board members, using board composition disclosures from proxy statements.
rationale: Higher dispersion may signal a mix of experience and fresh perspectives, improving governance and adaptability.
higher_returns_for: firms with high board tenure dispersion

name: Net Working Capital Turnover Growth
construction: Year-over-year percent change in (annual sales divided by average net working capital), using balance sheet and income statement data.
rationale: Increasing turnover may reflect improving operational efficiency and better capital allocation.
higher_returns_for: firms with high net working capital turnover growth

name: Segment Profit Margin Divergence
construction: Standard deviation of profit margins across business segments, as reported in annual segment disclosures.
rationale: High divergence may reveal hidden growth opportunities or risks in underperforming segments.
higher_returns_for: firms with high segment profit margin divergence

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Annual percentage change in R&D expenses (Compustat item XRD) over the last two fiscal years, divided by total assets (AT).
rationale: Firms with rapidly accelerating R&D spending may be investing in future growth opportunities not yet reflected in valuations.

name: Recent Insider Purchase Ratio
construction: Ratio of total shares purchased by insiders to total shares outstanding over the past 6 months (data from SEC Form 4 filings).
rationale: Insider purchases may signal undervaluation or positive private information about future firm prospects.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth Reversal
construction: Change in total assets (AT) over the last quarter, scaled by prior quarter assets, multiplied by -1.
rationale: Short-term asset growth may be negatively related to future returns due to overinvestment or mean reversion.

name: Cash Dividend Surprise
construction: Actual quarterly cash dividend per share minus the average quarterly dividend over the last two years.
rationale: Unexpected increases in dividends may signal management's confidence about future cash flows.

name: Deferred Tax Liability Growth
construction: Year-over-year percentage growth in deferred tax liabilities (Compustat TXDITC) scaled by total assets.
rationale: Rising deferred tax liabilities may indicate aggressive revenue recognition or early-stage asset growth.

name: Inventory Turnover Slope
construction: Slope of quarterly inventory turnover ratio (sales divided by average inventory; Compustat SALE/INVT) over the past 8 quarters.
rationale: Improvement in inventory management efficiency can precede better operating performance.

name: Net Share Repurchase Yield
construction: (Shares repurchased over the past year minus shares issued) divided by market capitalization.
rationale: Net share repurchases can signal undervaluation and shareholder-friendly capital allocation.

name: Accounts Receivable Divergence
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in accounts receivable (RECT) minus percentage change in sales (SALE).
rationale: Faster growth in receivables than sales may indicate aggressive revenue recognition or collection risk.

name: Operating Lease Obligations Ratio
construction: Estimated present value of operating lease obligations (from footnotes) divided by total assets.
rationale: High off-balance-sheet obligations may signal hidden financial risk and lower-quality earnings.

name: CEO Tenure Staleness
construction: Number of years since the CEO assumed office (from company proxy statements).
rationale: Long-tenured CEOs may be less adaptive and more entrenched, potentially leading to underperformance.

name: Customer Concentration Ratio
construction: Sum the percentage of total revenue derived from the firm's top 3 customers, as disclosed in annual filings.
rationale: Greater dependence on a few customers increases business risk and may not be fully priced.

name: Expense Deferral Ratio
construction: Calculate the ratio of capitalized expenses (e.g., capitalized R&D, software development costs) to total expenses in the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Firms deferring more expenses may be engaging in earnings management, which could signal future risk.

name: Insider Loan Guarantee Exposure
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if insiders have guaranteed company debt (disclosed in proxy or 10-K), 0 otherwise.
rationale: Insider financial commitment may signal alignment of interests and unpriced risk.

name: Short-Term Asset Volatility
construction: Compute standard deviation of quarterly changes in current assets over the past 12 quarters, scaled by average current assets.
rationale: Higher volatility in short-term assets may indicate operational uncertainty and mispricing.

name: Supplier Payment Stretch
construction: Change in days payable outstanding (DPO) over the past year.
rationale: Firms stretching payables may be facing financial constraints, which could foreshadow distress risk premium.

name: Cost of Goods Sold Smoothing
construction: Calculate the autocorrelation of quarterly cost of goods sold (COGS) over the past 12 quarters.
rationale: Higher autocorrelation may reflect earnings management or operational rigidity, both potentially underpriced.

name: Patent Citation Growth
construction: Annual growth rate in the number of patent citations disclosed in patent filings or annual reports.
rationale: Rising patent citations may capture future innovation unrecognized by the market.

name: Contingent Liability Density
construction: Sum of estimated contingent liabilities (e.g., pending litigation, environmental fines) as a percentage of total assets, as disclosed in notes to financial statements.
rationale: Firms with higher contingent liabilities may face unpriced risks that could result in higher required returns.

name: R&D Depreciation Ratio
construction: Ratio of accumulated amortization of capitalized R&D to total capitalized R&D on the balance sheet.
rationale: Higher ratios might signal mature or declining innovation assets, hence higher risk.

name: Non-GAAP Earnings Prevalence
construction: Count of non-GAAP earnings adjustments reported in press releases over the trailing year.
rationale: Frequent adjustments may indicate earnings quality concerns and hence higher risk premia.

name: Short-Term Operating Leverage Change
construction: Change in (Sales - Cost of Goods Sold) / Sales over the most recent quarter.
rationale: Firms with increasing operating leverage may experience greater earnings volatility, which could be rewarded with higher returns due to risk compensation.

name: Dividend Acceleration
construction: Growth rate of dividends per share over the past year relative to growth rate over the prior 3 years.
rationale: A sudden acceleration in dividend payments may signal management confidence and future profitability not yet priced in.

name: Inventory Write-down Frequency
construction: Number of inventory write-downs reported in the last three years.
rationale: Frequent inventory write-downs may indicate poor management or operational issues, while infrequent write-downs may reflect more stable operations.

name: Relative Analyst Forecast Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of analyst EPS forecasts divided by mean forecast for the next fiscal year.
rationale: High dispersion may indicate information uncertainty, which could be compensated with higher expected returns.

name: Insider Transaction Skew
construction: Sum of shares bought minus shares sold by insiders over the past 12 months, divided by total shares outstanding.
rationale: Net insider buying reflects management's private information and confidence in future prospects.

name: Industry-Relative R&D Growth
construction: Firm's growth rate of R&D spending over the last three years minus industry median R&D growth rate.
rationale: Firms ramping up R&D faster than peers may be investing in future competitiveness and innovation.

name: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift Amplifier
construction: Cumulative abnormal returns over 20 trading days following the last quarterly earnings announcement.
rationale: Firms with stronger post-earnings drift may experience persistent underreaction by the market.

name: Trade Credit Extension Ratio
construction: Accounts receivable divided by sales, relative to industry median.
rationale: Firms extending more trade credit than peers may be taking on extra risk to boost sales, potentially earning higher returns as a risk premium.
higher_returns_for: high trade credit extension relative to industry

name: Prior-Year Board Turnover
construction: Number of board of director changes in the prior year.
rationale: Higher board turnover may signal governance changes that precede operational improvements not yet priced in.

name: Employee Growth Surprise
construction: Current year employee headcount growth minus average annual growth over previous three years.
rationale: A sudden surge in hiring may indicate unanticipated expansion or positive demand shocks.

name: Short-Term Earnings Accrual Variability
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly earnings accruals (difference between net income and cash flow from operations) over the past 8 quarters, scaled by average total assets.
rationale: High variability in accruals may indicate earnings management or operational instability, which could be mispriced by investors.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high earnings accrual variability

name: Recent Employee Growth Rate
construction: Calculate the percentage change in the number of employees reported in the most recent annual report compared to 2 years prior.
rationale: Rapid changes in workforce may signal underlying shifts in firm growth prospects or over-expansion.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low recent employee growth rates

name: Supplier Concentration Ratio
construction: For firms disclosing their top 5 suppliers in 10-K filings, sum the percentage of total purchases attributed to those suppliers.
rationale: High supplier concentration may signal vulnerability to supply shocks or bargaining power issues, impacting future returns.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low supplier concentration ratios

name: Dividend Smoothing Persistence
construction: Measure the number of consecutive years with unchanged annual dividends per share over the past decade.
rationale: Persistent dividend smoothing may signal conservative management and information asymmetry.
higher_returns_for: stocks with longer streaks of unchanged dividends

name: Deferred Tax Asset Growth
construction: Calculate the percentage change in deferred tax assets over the trailing 3 years, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Aggressive use of deferred tax assets may indicate earnings management or lower future profitability.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low deferred tax asset growth

name: Off-Balance Sheet Operating Leases
construction: Estimate the present value of future minimum lease payments for operating leases, scaled by total assets, using footnote disclosures.
rationale: High off-balance sheet leverage may be underappreciated by the market and signal higher risk.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high off-balance sheet operating leases

name: Related Party Transaction Intensity
construction: Count the number of related party transactions disclosed in the most recent 10-K, standardized by total assets.
rationale: Frequent related party transactions may reflect weak governance and potential for misappropriation, affecting returns.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low related party transaction intensity

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: For firms that capitalize R&D, calculate the ratio of capitalized R&D to total reported R&D over the past 3 years.
rationale: A high ratio may indicate aggressive capitalization and overstatement of assets, affecting future returns.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low R&D capitalization ratios

name: Seasonal Inventory Build-up
construction: Measure the average change in inventory from Q3 to Q4 over the past 5 years, scaled by total annual sales.
rationale: Predictable seasonal inventory swings may indicate inefficient inventory management or exposure to demand shocks.
higher_returns_for: stocks with low seasonal inventory build-up

name: Pre-announcement Drift
construction: Calculate the average abnormal return in the 30 days before quarterly earnings announcements over the past 4 quarters.
rationale: Stocks with consistent pre-announcement drift may be subject to information leakage or sentiment-driven price moves.
higher_returns_for: stocks with high positive pre-announcement drift

name: Long-Term Asset Growth Volatility
construction: Calculate the standard deviation of annual percent changes in total assets over the past 7 years using Compustat annual data.
rationale: Firms with stable growth in assets may reflect disciplined capital allocation, while volatile asset growth could signal inconsistent strategy or response to industry shocks.

name: Cash Flow Persistence
construction: Regress quarterly operating cash flows on a constant over the past 16 quarters; use the R-squared as the measure.
rationale: Persistent cash flows suggest a more predictable and durable business model, which may be underappreciated by the market.

name: Relative Supplier Concentration
construction: Divide purchases from the top supplier (from 10-K supply chain disclosures) by total COGS in the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Dependence on a single supplier can expose firms to operational risks that might not be priced in.

name: Cumulative Insider Trading Net Value
construction: Sum net purchases (buys minus sells) by all insiders over the past 12 months from SEC Form 4 filings, scaled by market capitalization.
rationale: Insiders have superior information about future firm prospects and their net buying may signal undervaluation.

name: Dividend Smoothing Score
construction: Standard deviation of annual dividend per share changes over the past 10 years, divided by average earnings per share over the same period.
rationale: Stable dividend policies may indicate management confidence and financial discipline, attracting longer-term investors.

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: Ratio of accumulated R&D expense over the past 5 years to total assets, with R&D accumulated as if it were capitalized and depreciated linearly over 5 years.
rationale: Firms investing heavily in R&D may be underappreciated if the market treats R&D as an expense rather than an investment.

name: Patent Application Intensity
construction: Count of patent applications in the past 3 years from USPTO data, divided by total assets.
rationale: High rates of innovation may drive future profitability that is not yet reflected in accounting numbers.

name: Lagged Environmental Incident Count
construction: Count the number of reported environmental violations or incidents (from EPA records) in the prior 3 years.
rationale: Firms with poor environmental track records may face regulatory or reputational risks not fully priced in.

name: Supplier Payment Delay Index
construction: Average days payable outstanding (DPO) over the past 3 years, from Compustat cash flow and balance sheet data.
rationale: Firms delaying payments to suppliers might be experiencing liquidity issues or extracting value from working capital at the cost of long-term relationships.

name: Relative Geographic Expansion Rate
construction: Count of new international markets entered in the last 5 years (as disclosed in 10-K business segment information), divided by prior 5-year average firm sales.
rationale: Aggressive but successful geographic expansion may signal growth opportunities yet to be fully priced.

name: Insider Net Buying Ratio
construction: Sum of all insider (officers and directors) open-market share purchases over the past 12 months minus insider sales, divided by total shares outstanding.
rationale: Insiders may have superior information on firm prospects; net buyers may signal undervaluation or impending positive developments.

name: Patent Intensity
construction: Number of new US patents granted to the firm in the previous year divided by total assets at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Firms with high rates of innovation may be better positioned for future growth and profitability.

name: Voluntary Disclosure Frequency
construction: Count of press releases related to new products, earnings guidance, or strategy (excluding mandatory SEC filings) issued by the firm over the prior 12 months.
rationale: Frequent voluntary disclosures may signal management confidence and transparency, attracting investor interest.

name: Employee Efficiency Ratio
construction: Total revenue over the past fiscal year divided by the number of employees (from 10-K filings).
rationale: Firms generating more revenue per employee may be more operationally efficient and profitable.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth
construction: Percentage change in cash and short-term investments over the past fiscal year.
rationale: Rapid growth in liquid assets may reflect asset redeployment or underutilization, potentially predicting lower future returns if not matched by investment.

name: Dividend Initiation Indicator
construction: Binary variable set to 1 if a firm initiates a regular cash dividend within the last 12 months, 0 otherwise.
rationale: The decision to begin paying dividends may signal management’s confidence in sustainable earnings.

name: Customer Concentration Risk
construction: Percentage of total sales accounted for by the largest single customer, as disclosed in 10-K filings.
rationale: Firms highly dependent on a single customer may face greater earnings risk and discounting by investors.

name: Deferred Tax Asset Ratio
construction: Deferred tax assets divided by total assets at fiscal year-end.
rationale: Large deferred tax assets may indicate aggressive accounting or expectations of future losses, which could foreshadow poorer performance.

name: Earnings Announcement Drift Sensitivity
construction: Stock’s average abnormal return over 3-day windows around the past four quarterly earnings announcements.
rationale: Stocks that strongly react to earnings surprises may have more persistent mispricing or information inefficiency.

name: R&D-to-Sales Change
construction: Year-over-year change in R&D expense divided by prior year total sales.
rationale: Increasing R&D intensity may indicate management commitment to innovation and future growth.

name: Short-Term Accrual Volatility
construction: Calculate the standard deviation of quarterly short-term accruals (change in current assets minus change in current liabilities, scaled by average total assets) over the past 8 quarters.
rationale: Firms with volatile accruals may face greater uncertainty in earnings quality, which could be mispriced by investors.

name: R&D Intensity Change
construction: Compute the year-over-year percentage change in R&D expense divided by total assets.
rationale: Firms increasing R&D intensity may be investing in future growth opportunities not yet recognized by the market.

name: Dividend Initiation Momentum
construction: Indicator variable equal to 1 if a firm initiated a dividend in the past 12 months and 0 otherwise.
rationale: Dividend initiations may signal management confidence and improved future prospects.

name: Inventory Write-Down Frequency
construction: Count the number of inventory write-downs disclosed in annual reports over the past 5 years.
rationale: Frequent write-downs may indicate poor inventory management or persistent operational issues.

name: Relative Insider Net Buying
construction: Sum net insider purchases (purchases minus sales) over the past 6 months, scaled by shares outstanding.
rationale: Insider buying may reflect private information about undervaluation or positive future developments.

name: Patent Application Growth
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in the number of patent applications filed by the firm, as reported in public filings.
rationale: Rising patent activity may signal innovation and future competitive advantage.

name: Deferred Tax Asset Ratio
construction: Deferred tax assets divided by total assets, as reported in the most recent annual report.
rationale: High deferred tax assets may indicate aggressive accounting or future earnings headwinds.

name: Customer Concentration Risk
construction: Percentage of total sales to the firm's largest customer, as disclosed in annual filings.
rationale: High customer concentration exposes firms to idiosyncratic risk that may not be fully priced.

name: Seasonal Sales Growth Consistency
construction: Standard deviation of year-over-year quarterly sales growth rates for the same quarter over the past 4 years.
rationale: Consistent seasonal sales growth may indicate stable demand and operational strength.

name: Unrecognized Pension Liability Ratio
construction: Unrecognized pension liabilities divided by market capitalization, as disclosed in footnotes of annual reports.
rationale: Large unrecognized pension liabilities may represent hidden financial risk.

name: Inventory Adjustment Ratio
construction: Annual change in inventories divided by prior year total assets, using Compustat INVT and AT items.
rationale: Firms rapidly increasing inventories may face future write-downs or demand misestimation, while those controlling inventories may have superior operational efficiency.

name: Deferred Tax Liability Growth
construction: One-year change in deferred tax liabilities (Compustat TXDITC) divided by average total assets.
rationale: Growth in deferred tax liabilities may indicate aggressive earnings management or temporary tax benefits that could reverse, affecting future performance.

name: Supplier Concentration Risk
construction: Estimated from 10-K segment disclosures, the proportion of total purchases from the top 3 suppliers.
rationale: Firms relying heavily on few suppliers may face higher operational risks, reducing expected returns.

name: Short-Term Lease Commitment Ratio
construction: Total future minimum lease payments due within one year (from footnotes) divided by current assets.
rationale: High short-term lease obligations may signal liquidity risk or near-term cost pressures.

name: Employee Productivity Change
construction: One-year change in sales per employee, using Compustat SALE and EMP data.
rationale: Firms improving productivity may enjoy competitive advantages leading to better future returns.

name: Patent Filing Intensity
construction: Count of patents filed in past year divided by total assets, as reported in 10-Ks and USPTO filings.
rationale: High patent intensity may signal innovation and future growth prospects not fully priced by the market.

name: Working Capital Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly net working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) over the past three years, scaled by average total assets.
rationale: Greater volatility in working capital may indicate uncertain cash flows and operational instability.

name: Board Meeting Frequency
construction: Number of board meetings held in the prior fiscal year, as disclosed in proxy statements.
rationale: More frequent board meetings could reflect heightened oversight, potentially improving governance and firm performance.

name: Foreign Income Share
construction: Proportion of income before extraordinary items (Compustat IB) generated by foreign subsidiaries, as disclosed in segment data.
rationale: Firms with higher foreign income may benefit from geographic diversification and access to growth markets.

name: R&D Capitalization Ratio
construction: Capitalized R&D (if allowed) divided by total R&D expenditure (Compustat XRD) over the past three years.
rationale: A higher ratio may suggest management’s confidence in the future payoff of R&D investments.

name: Inventory Volatility Ratio
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly inventory levels (Compustat item INVT) over the past 12 quarters, scaled by average inventory over the same period.
rationale: Firms with more volatile inventories may face higher uncertainty and risk, which could be compensated with higher returns.

name: Advertising Expense Intensity Change
construction: Annual change in advertising expenses (Compustat item XAD) divided by lagged total assets (Compustat item AT), measured over the most recent fiscal year.
rationale: Increasing advertising intensity may signal growth investment not yet priced in by the market.

name: Long-Term Debt Growth Acceleration
construction: Second difference (acceleration) of long-term debt (Compustat item DLTT) over the past three fiscal years, divided by total assets.
rationale: Accelerating debt issuance may precede significant investment or expansion that the market undervalues.

name: Net Working Capital to Market Value
construction: Net working capital (current assets minus current liabilities, Compustat items ACT - LCT) divided by market capitalization (CRSP).
rationale: Firms with high working capital relative to market value could be undervalued or more financially flexible.

name: Gross Margin Seasonality
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly gross margin percentage (gross profit / sales, Compustat items GP/Sale) over the past 12 quarters.
rationale: Firms with less predictable gross margins may be riskier but potentially offer higher returns as compensation.

name: Industry Sales Dispersion
construction: Firm's annual sales (Compustat item SALE) minus the mean sales of its industry (4-digit SIC), divided by industry sales standard deviation.
rationale: Outlier firms in terms of sales—especially on the high side—might be mispriced due to insufficient peer comparables.
higher_returns_for: high positive or negative values of the measure

name: R&D Consistency Score
construction: Number of consecutive years with nonzero R&D expense (Compustat item XRD) over the past 10 years.
rationale: Sustained R&D investment could signal long-term innovation, which markets tend to undervalue.

name: Unrecognized Asset Growth
construction: Annual change in off-balance sheet operating leases (from footnote disclosures) divided by total assets.
rationale: Growing off-balance sheet assets may indicate hidden investments not fully incorporated into equity prices.

name: Share Repurchase Frequency
construction: Number of quarterly reductions in shares outstanding (Compustat item CSHO) over the past 12 quarters.
rationale: Frequent buybacks may reflect management signaling undervaluation or commitment to shareholder returns.

name: Patent Grant Momentum
construction: Number of new patents granted (from USPTO records matched by firm) in the past 12 months minus the previous 12 months, divided by total assets.
rationale: Increasing patent activity may precede new product launches and future earnings surprises.

name: Short-Term Asset Growth Dispersion
construction: Compute the standard deviation of quarterly asset growth rates over the past two years for each firm.
rationale: Firms with highly volatile asset growth may reflect managerial uncertainty or shifting business prospects, potentially mispriced by investors.

name: R&D to Free Cash Flow Ratio
construction: Divide total R&D expense (annual) by free cash flow (annual, operating cash flow minus capital expenditures).
rationale: Firms investing a higher proportion of free cash flow into R&D may have more growth options underappreciated by the market.

name: Late Filer Indicator
construction: Flag firms that file annual 10-Ks more than 90 days after fiscal year-end.
rationale: Late filings may signal internal problems or poor governance that investors penalize, possibly leading to subsequent mean reversion.

name: Net Insider Trading
construction: Sum net insider purchases (shares bought minus shares sold by officers/directors) over the past six months and divide by shares outstanding.
rationale: Insiders have superior firm information; net purchases may indicate undervaluation.

name: Negative Analyst Revision Skew
construction: Calculate the skewness of analyst earnings forecast revisions over the past year for each firm.
rationale: Unusually negative skewness may indicate overreaction, leading to future reversals.

name: Operating Cost Stickiness
construction: Measure percent change in operating costs when revenue falls by at least 5% year-over-year; define stickiness as % cost change divided by % revenue change.
rationale: Firms with stickier costs may have less operational flexibility, which could be mispriced by the market.

name: New Product Announcements
construction: Count the number of new product launches announced in press releases in the past 12 months.
rationale: Frequent product launches may reflect innovation undervalued by investors.

name: Backlog Growth Rate
construction: Compute the year-over-year percentage change in order backlog as reported in 10-Ks.
rationale: Rising backlogs can signal underestimated future revenues and growth.

name: Dividend Initiation Surprise
construction: Flag firms that initiate a dividend after at least three years of no dividend; measure the amount as a percent of current earnings.
rationale: Unexpected dividend initiations may signal improved prospects underappreciated by the market.

name: Patent Citation Intensity
construction: Count the number of citations received by a firm’s patents (from USPTO data) over the past three years, scaled by total assets.
rationale: Firms with more highly cited patents may possess valuable intellectual property not fully reflected in current prices.

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Year-over-year percentage change in total number of employees, using headcount data from annual 10-K filings.
rationale: Rapid expansion in workforce may signal overinvestment or managerial over-optimism, while stable or declining employment could indicate operational discipline.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative employee growth rate

name: Short-Term Asset Turnover Surge
construction: The change in asset turnover ratio (sales divided by average total assets) from the previous year to the current year.
rationale: A sudden increase in asset turnover may capture temporary efficiency improvements or aggressive revenue recognition, potentially reversing.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative recent changes in asset turnover

name: Unrecognized Pension Obligation Ratio
construction: Unrecognized pension obligations scaled by total assets, extracted from pension footnotes in 10-K filings.
rationale: Large unrecognized pension liabilities create future cash flow drags that may not yet be priced.
higher_returns_for: firms with low unrecognized pension obligation ratios

name: Interim Inventory Swings
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly inventory levels over the trailing four quarters, divided by average inventory over that period.
rationale: Volatile inventory levels may indicate weak demand forecasting or channel stuffing risk.

name: Option-Implied Volatility Slope
construction: Difference between implied volatilities of 3-month and 6-month at-the-money call options, using listed equity options data.
rationale: A steeply upward sloping term structure of implied volatility may indicate upcoming firm-specific risk that is not yet reflected in analyst coverage.
higher_returns_for: firms with low or negative implied volatility slope

name: Segment Revenue Dispersion
construction: Standard deviation of revenue growth rates across reported business segments, taken from annual segment disclosures.
rationale: Firms with highly dispersed segment growth may face internal resource allocation issues or be more exposed to sector-specific shocks.
higher_returns_for: firms with low revenue dispersion across segments

name: Excess R&D to SG&A
construction: Current year R&D expense divided by SG&A expense, minus median ratio for the firm's industry.
rationale: Excess R&D investment relative to peers may reflect overconfidence or indicate less near-term profitability.
higher_returns_for: firms with below-industry-median R&D to SG&A ratios

name: Cash Tax Gap
construction: Difference between effective cash tax rate (cash taxes paid divided by pretax income) and statutory federal tax rate.
rationale: A large negative gap can reveal aggressive tax avoidance or exposure to one-off tax benefits that may not persist.
higher_returns_for: firms with small or positive cash tax gaps

name: Net Insider Transaction Ratio
construction: Net shares bought minus shares sold by insiders over the past 12 months, divided by shares outstanding, using SEC Form 4 filings.
rationale: High net insider selling can reflect adverse private information about future prospects.
higher_returns_for: firms with high net insider buying ratios

name: Late Filing Frequency
construction: Number of late quarterly or annual SEC filings in the past three years.
rationale: Frequent late filings may signal internal control weaknesses or hidden operational problems.
higher_returns_for: firms with zero or few late filings

name: R&D Acceleration
construction: Year-over-year change in R&D expenditure (Compustat item XRD) as a percentage of total assets (AT), calculated as: [(R&D_t / AT_t) - (R&D_{t-1} / AT_{t-1})].
rationale: Firms accelerating investment in research and development may be positioning for future growth that is not yet recognized by the market.

name: Net Insider Share Purchases
construction: Total net shares purchased by insiders (Form 4 filings) over the past 12 months, scaled by shares outstanding (Compustat item CSHO).
rationale: Significant insider buying relative to company size may signal undervaluation or positive private information.

name: Earnings Announcement Drift Sensitivity
construction: Regression beta of a stock's returns to the market's reaction to recent earnings surprises for its sector, measured over the prior 8 quarters.
rationale: Stocks more sensitive to sector-wide earnings surprise reactions may be underpriced for their informational efficiency or future revaluation.

name: Short-Term Asset Turnover Change
construction: Difference in asset turnover (sales/total assets, Compustat items SALE/AT) between the last fiscal year and the prior year.
rationale: Increasing efficiency in asset utilization may precede improvements in profitability and future returns.

name: Employee Growth Rate
construction: Percentage change in number of employees (Compustat item EMP) from the previous fiscal year.
rationale: Rapid hiring may signal management's confidence in future demand and expansion opportunities.

name: Dividend Omission Signal
construction: Indicator for firms that have recently omitted or suspended a regular dividend (annual Compustat dividend per share DPS data), but were previously consistent payers.
rationale: Market overreaction to dividend cuts may lead to undervaluation for firms undergoing temporary distress or restructuring.

name: Patent Application Intensity
construction: Number of new US patent applications filed in the past year (USPTO data), scaled by total assets.
rationale: High rates of patent application may indicate future product launches and innovative capacity not reflected in current valuation.

name: Cash Flow Seasonality
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly operating cash flow (Compustat item OANCF) over the past 8 quarters, divided by average quarterly cash flow over the same period.
rationale: Lower seasonality in cash flows may indicate more stable business models and risk underestimation by the market.

name: Supplier Concentration Exposure
construction: Sum of revenue percentages derived from top 3 suppliers as disclosed in 10-K filings, or as available from FactSet Supply Chain data.
rationale: Greater revenue concentration may expose firms to risks not fully priced in, or may reflect bargaining power and cost advantages.

name: Deferred Tax Asset Growth
construction: Year-over-year change in deferred tax assets (Compustat item DTAS), scaled by lagged total assets (AT).
rationale: Rising deferred tax assets may signal aggressive tax planning or future profitability that is underappreciated by the market.

name: Customer Concentration Ratio
construction: Sum the percentage of total revenue derived from the firm's top 3 customers, as disclosed in annual filings (10-K).
rationale: Firms highly dependent on a few customers may face higher cash flow risk, which could be priced in expected returns.

name: Patent Intensity
construction: Number of new patents granted in the past fiscal year divided by total assets, using USPTO data and firm disclosures.
rationale: Firms with intense patent activity may signal innovation and future growth potential not captured by traditional measures.

name: Quarterly Earnings Volatility
construction: Standard deviation of quarterly earnings per share (EPS) over the past 8 quarters.
rationale: High earnings volatility may indicate risk or mispricing associated with informational uncertainty.

name: Insider Net Purchase Ratio
